Q: pgrep does not search for long (more than 15 chars) process name A:

If you want to grep for a process with the exact name core-plugin-loader and disregard its command line arguments, you can use this:

pkill --full '^core-plugin-loader($| )'

This will match command lines such as:

  • core-plugin-loader --file=/usr/lib/blah.so
  • core-plugin-loader

But won't match core-plugin-loader-unrelated

pkill without --full uses the process name stored in /proc/<pid>/comm which is limited to 15 characters.

pkill with --full uses /proc/<pid>/cmdline instead which doesn't have that limitation.

Q: Why does my Pod stay in ImagePullBackOff after I just ran docker build locally, when the exact same tag exists in my local Docker daemon? A:

This is a common misconception. Simply put, your host Docker daemon and the k3d cluster do not share an image store.

Your command - docker build -t myapp:dev . - puts the image in the host Docker daemon. k3d runs Kubernetes nodes as containers, and those nodes use their own containerd image stores. So, the kubelet asks the node’s container runtime for myapp:dev and that runtime does not have it. Hence, so Kubernetes treats the unqualified name as docker.io/library/myapp:dev and tries Docker Hub.

What you can do is import the image into k3d, then import it. After that, restart your deployment.

k3d cluster list  
k3d image import myapp:dev --cluster \<cluster-name\>  
kubectl rollout restart deployment/myapp  
kubectl rollout status deployment/myapp

Ideally, you would want to set up a local registry. You can read more on that here.

Q: Is it worth using Twitter Bootstrap for a fully customised responsive design A:

Hate to plug my own work (that's a lie) but my framework Jeet is perfect for this. Seems like you just need a solid responsive grid system so if you're not afraid of Stylus I invite you to fork this CodePen and toy around with it.

If it's not your cup of tea or you're more comfortable with other preprocessors (SCSS particularly) then I'd suggest Bourbon's Neat for a simple grid, or Singularity.gs for a really powerful grid.

Either way I'd suggest against "padding-based" grids like Bootstrap 3 and Foundation 4 as they essentially force you to create/nest extra elements inside of every element just for transparent gutters (something very common). It turns into way too much bloat.

Q: Does a template for asp.net mvc 4 built on the Semantic UI framework exist? A:

No, it doesn't exist out-of-box, but you are free to create your own template. The templates for MVC in both 5 (VS 2013) and 6 (VS 2015 preview) are also using Bootstrap.

Alternatively, you can add the NuGet package to your project (though, it does not seem to be an official project package):

PM> Install-Package SemanticUI.ASP.NET.MVC
